title: When Leverage Replaces Growth
content:
When Leverage Replaces Growth
China’s margin financing just hit a record at around $390B, above the 2015 peak. The easy read is retail is back, bubble vibes, here we go again. 
But if you layer in what China actually looks like underneath..property still wounded, private demand still weak, producer prices still soft..the margin spike starts to look less like confidence!and more like a system searching for somewhere to put risk.
Leverage Can Rise Because the Economy Is Weak
In a healthy cycle, borrowing grows because people want to invest, expand, hire, build.
In a balance!sheet recession, borrowing can grow for a different reason..there aren’t many places left that feel like they work.
If property is broken as a wealth engine and household confidence is shaky, money doesn’t magically become productive. It tends to migrate into the one arena that still offers the feeling of upside..the stock market.
So margin debt here isn’t just risk appetite. It’s also lack of alternatives.
The Market Starts Being Set by Forced Flows
Once leverage becomes a big part of the buyer base, the market stops behaving like a normal fundamentals and positioning story and starts behaving like a reflexive machine..
As prices rise, borrowing increases. More borrowing fuels more buying, which pushes prices higher again and the cycle keeps reinforcing itself until something finally breaks the momentum.
And when it stalls, margin doesn’t unwind politely. It unwinds through forced selling, and in markets like China’s with heavier retail participation, less natural shorting, and more policy signaling those moves can get jumpy fast.
That’s why I pay less attention to the record and more attention to the role margin is playing in setting the marginal price.
This Looks Like Substitution Not Mania
If you’re Beijing and property can’t carry confidence the way it used to, you have a problem..you need stability without a traditional wealth!effect engine.
One way out is to quietly let equities become a replacement confidence channel not because it’s ideal, but because it’s available.
That doesn’t mean they want a 2015 style blowoff. It means they want something more controlled: enough upside to stabilize sentiment, not so much leverage that the market becomes ungovernable.
Which is why policy tweaks and regulatory tightening matter here more than the headline number. In China, the put exists but it comes with conditions.
Deflation at Home, Pressure Abroad
A weak domestic engine doesn’t stay domestic forever. If China can’t reflate consumption cleanly, the natural outlet is exports..push volume outward, keep factories running, preserve employment.
That’s how a deflationary problem at home turns into trade friction abroad. The rest of the world feels the pressure through cheaper goods, squeezed margins, and political backlash. That’s where tariffs, restrictions, and second China shock!talk comes from.
So this margin story isn’t isolated. It’s part of a bigger regime..internal weakness, external pressure.
Where This Take Could Be Wrong
Two big ways this framing collapses..
1.   If property stabilizes faster than expected and domestic confidence genuinely returns, margin debt could just be a normal cyclical upswing.
2.   If today’s leverage is more institutional and hedged and less shadowy than 2015, the crash risk analogy could be overstated.
My View
Record margin debt in a deflation leaning China isn’t a clean bull signal. It’s a sign that risk is being rerouted from a broken property channel into equities because the system needs a place to manufacture confidence.
That can work for a while. But it also means the market becomes more fragile, more policy dependent, and more prone to air pockets if momentum breaks.
If you want one thing to keep an eye on..watch whether Beijing keeps tightening around leverage while still trying to keep the tape supported. That’s the line between managed substitution and another reflexive unwind.<code[...]

title: one thing I've learned, and continue to learn
content:
one thing I've learned, and continue to learn
never bet against people. doesn't matter who it is...don't do it.
first, walking around the battlefield and helping people up is just a far better way to go thru life. puts you on the right side of God, humanity, and love...a Pascalian wager that keeps you optimistic and has you expending the same energy into the universe that you'd want to receive
second, life is long and ppl will surprise you. Plutarch's Moralia has a Lives-esque chapter on famed warriors who ran way too hot in their 20's/30's but then settled into final form, perfected their character & made history...the duality of man, Jung's "the brighter the light, the darker the shadow."
third, to short "human capital" is akin to shorting a levered equity with no stop. as the quote goes, "he who has one enemy will meet him everywhere"...especially if the dude is spiteful, like a Kobe type, where they take pleasure in stopping by to twist the knife in you every single day.
I don't operate that way, but at the same time, looking back... I've had days where the future looked bleak as fuck. then some mf throws some disrespect your way, and it ends up being exactly what breathes new life into you. 
God will send you motivation in unusual forms...so love your critics man, sometimes they're the perfect source of fuel.
the question you probably want to ask:
“What if I bet on someone and I'm wrong?” 
Type 1 and type 2 errors, brotha...los dos, siempre. pick which direction you want to be wrong in, bc you're going to be wrong.
I think you'll not only be wrong more often in betting against people, but you'll find yourself in severe pain each and every day...just like Baltasar Gracian wrote, how "the envious die not one death, but as often as the envied win applause."
but look, I ain't gonna argue with ya. keep kicking people while they're down...you can be over there and I'll be over here. good luck and God bless

title: The TLT Accumulation Story Sounds Right… Until You...
content:
The TLT Accumulation Story Sounds Right… Until You Zoom Out
I get why people are excited about TLT. It’s been a disaster since 2020, it’s finally stopped falling, and yields are high enough that you’re getting paid to wait. When something is that hated and it stops making new lows, the bottom is in narrative starts to feel obvious.
But the clean version of this story skips the part that matters most..why long bonds would rally from here.
What the Chart Is Really Saying
The chart mostly says we’ve moved from falling knife!to stabilizing. That’s not nothing. Bases often form when nobody wants the asset and the selling pressure just runs out of energy.
But a base isn’t the same thing as a new uptrend. Right now it’s more like..the market stopped panicking. It hasn’t started believing again.
Volume Doesn’t Automatically Mean Institutions Are Loading Up 
This is where I think people get fooled.
TLT isn’t a normal investment product. It’s a macro tool. A lot of the trading is hedges, options flows, relative value trades, people rotating risk, people putting on duration as protection, then taking it off again.
So heavy volume can mean institutions are involved, sure but it doesn’t automatically mean institutions are accumulating a long.
If you want a cleaner read on accumulation, you look at flows. And lately, shares outstanding have actually been drifting lower. More people have been pulling money out than putting new money in. That’s not what quiet conviction buying looks like.
The Real Bet Here Isn’t Technical It’s Macro
The post leans on a familiar rule..when the 10 year peaks, long bonds usually rip.
That worked great in the 2010s. But we’re not in the 2010s.
Today, long rates aren’t just about growth and inflation. They’re also about supply, deficits, and term premium..the extra yield investors demand for holding long duration in a world that feels less stable.
So it’s totally possible for the Fed to ease, the front end to fall… and the long end to stay sticky because investors still want to be paid for the risk.
That’s the regime shift people keep underestimating.
What Those Price Targets Really Imply
Calling for $115–$140 sounds like sentiment turning. But it’s really a bigger claim than that.
To get a move like that, you usually need one of two things..
•   a real growth and credit shock that forces a classic flight to safety, or
•   some form of policy support that directly benefits long duration (think balance sheet tools, not just rate cuts)
Either way, the bonds rally hard because something else is breaking or the rules of the game are being changed.
So the upside is real but it’s not free.
Where This Take Could Be Wrong
If we get a genuine disinflation pulse, growth rolls over, and the market starts pricing a deeper easing cycle, TLT can absolutely rip. In that scenario, today’s prices will look like a gift.
But if the next phase is more fiscal, supply and geopolitics that’ll keep term premium elevated, then TLT might just chop sideways… or disappoint again.
That’s the fork in the road.
My View
I don’t hate TLT here. As paid insurance, it finally makes sense again. You’re earning yield while you wait, and if a real slowdown hits, you’ve got convexity.
But I wouldn’t confuse it stopped going down with it’s about to do 30–50%. That’s not a chart call. That’s a macro call.
The real question is simple..is the next shock deflationary… or is it the bond market demanding a higher price for long term risk?
Answer that, and you’ll know whether this base is a launchpad or just a pause.

title: Why Raising Kids Well Is Really About What Happens...
content:
Why Raising Kids Well Is Really About What Happens Later
Raising kids right isn’t about getting through the next day smoothly. It’s about building someone who can handle life when you’re not in the room..when they’re stressed, tempted, disappointed, or suddenly successful. That’s the part people don’t see while it’s happening. You’re not just shaping behavior. You’re shaping how a future adult relates to responsibility, effort, money, and truth.
That’s also why parenting shows up so clearly in what happens to wealth across generations.
What the Data Says About Generational Wealth
There’s a reason the phrase “shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves in three generations” exists across cultures. Long term studies tracking family wealth show a consistent pattern…
•   By the second generation, roughly 70% of families have lost most or all of the original wealth.
•   By the third generation, close to 90% is gone.
What surprises most people is why. It’s rarely bad markets or poor investing. Research consistently shows that wealth usually fails because of family dynamics..breakdowns in communication, trust, preparation, and shared purpose.
In other words, wealth doesn’t disappear financially first. It disappears personally.
Presence Is The Foundation
What kids need first is simple but not easy..they need you. Not in a helicopter way but in a steady, consistent way. Time with your kids isn’t a parenting trick. It’s how trust is built.
That matters later more than almost anything else. When they mess up or feel unsure, the real question isn’t “Do they know the right answer?” It’s “Do they feel safe enough to tell the truth?” Families that fall apart later rarely do so because of one big event. They fall apart slowly, as communication shuts down and trust erodes.
And once trust is gone, money tends to make things worse.
Kids Learn Character by Watching
Kids don’t learn character from speeches. They learn it by watching how you live. When they see you work..not just talk about work..they absorb commitment, consistency, and responsibility.
They learn that showing up matters, even when it’s boring or unglamorous. That turns into grit later. It becomes the ability to stay in a marriage during a rough season, build a career patiently, and handle setbacks without becoming bitter or entitled.
Let Them Struggle Without Abandoning Them
Letting kids struggle a little matters. Not neglect. Not harsh tough love. Just enough friction so they don’t collapse the first time life doesn’t bend.
Remove every consequence and you raise a fragile adult. Demand too much without warmth and you raise anxiety. The balance is standards with support..I believe in you, and I’m not rescuing you from everything.
That’s how resilience is built.
What Excellence Actually Means
Demanding excellence doesn’t mean demanding perfection. It means ownership. Doing what you said you’d do. Telling the truth when it costs you. Finishing what you start.
That kind of excellence compounds because it makes people reliable. And reliable people get trusted. Trusted people get opportunities..in work, relationships, leadership, and eventually, wealth.
Where Parenting and Wealth Collide
Most fortunes don’t disappear because of taxes or bad advice. They disappear because heirs aren’t prepared, families don’t share a mission, and trust fractures once money enters the room.
Families that preserve wealth tend to do the unglamorous work early..values, communication, preparation, shared purpose. That work doesn’t start in an estate plan. It starts at the dinner table, long before money ever changes hands.
The Real Goal
Spend time with your kids. Let them see you work. Let them struggle a bit. Expect a lot from them.
Raise someone who can handle freedom without self destructing, and responsibility without resenting it. Because one day, whether it’s money, leadership, or just their own life, it will be their turn and you want them ready when it is.

title: U.S. Housing Update..Demand Is Collapsing, But Pri...
content:
U.S. Housing Update..Demand Is Collapsing, But Prices Aren’t the Whole Story
What The Data Just Told Us
Pending home sales fell to 71.8 in December, down 9.3% month over month, with mortgage rates averaging about 6.2%. That’s not a seasonal wobble..it’s a clear signal that affordability is still doing the damage. The monthly payment, not the sticker price, is what’s keeping buyers on the sidelines.
The Freeze Most People Miss
Housing isn’t cracking the way it usually does because supply isn’t responding. A huge share of homeowners are locked into ultra low mortgage rates from prior years, so they don’t list unless they absolutely have to. That keeps inventory thin, limits choices, and leaves buyers stuck with the worst mix..high financing costs and very little to buy. Even as closings tick up in spots, new listings aren’t keeping pace, which continues to suppress contract activity.
Why Prices Falling Is Too Simple
Markets don’t clear through one lever. Housing adjusts through some combination of..
•   Lower rates
•   Lower prices
•   More supply
A lot of the adjustment can happen quietly..time, inflation, and selective price cuts in overheated metros while tighter markets simply go sideways. The real risk in 2026 isn’t today’s price level, it’s volume. If low transaction activity starts spilling into the broader economy..brokers, lenders, local tax revenues, labor mobility and the labor market weakens, that’s when forced selling breaks the lock in and turns a frozen market into a real price event.
What To Watch Next
•   Inventory levels
•   Mortgage rate spreads (not just headline rates)
•   Unemployment and layoffs
Prices can stagnate longer than people expect. Jobs are the tripwire that changes everything.

title: Reading Between the Lines of the Personal Income &...
content:
Reading Between the Lines of the Personal Income & Outlays Report (Nov 2025)
Income is rising, spending is holding up, and inflation appears contained. That’s the surface read.
Underneath, the structure tells a more fragile story where consumption is increasingly outpacing income, savings are being drawn down, and some of the inflation calm rests on imperfect data due to the government shutdown. The economy isn’t breaking but it’s running with less margin for error.
The Headline Numbers (What Everyone Sees)
Month over month (November)..
•   Personal income: +0.3%
•   Disposable personal income (DPI): +0.3%
•   Personal consumption expenditures (PCE): +0.5%
•   Real PCE (inflation adjusted): +0.3%
•   Core PCE inflation: +0.2%
Year over year…
•   Nominal PCE: +5.4%
•   Real PCE: +2.6%
•   Core PCE inflation: +2.8%
On paper, this supports the “steady growth, cooling inflation” narrative.
Spending Is Running Ahead of Income
The more important relationship is spending versus income…
•   Real disposable income is up only 1.0% YoY
•   Real consumption is up 2.6% YoY
That gap matters. It means households are not primarily funding consumption with rising real income. They’re bridging the difference elsewhere.
Savings Is The Silent Pressure Point
•   Personal saving rate fell to 3.5% in November
•   Down from 5.5% earlier in 2025
•   Near the lowest levels seen since late 2022
This isn’t precautionary saving. Confidence surveys are weak, not euphoric. The decline in savings is best read as buffer depletion, not optimism.
When savings are low, the economy becomes more sensitive to…
•   Job losses
•   Credit tightening
•   Energy or food price shocks
Revisions Matter More Than the New Print
Because of the shutdown, BEA released October and November together and revised July September at the same time.
Those revisions quietly changed the backdrop…
•   Prior income growth was revised lower
•   Prior spending was revised higher
•   Personal saving was revised down sharply
In plain terms..households entered the fall with less income momentum and less savings than previously thought, while spending was already stronger.

🍫
 Cocoa At A 2 Year Low And What the Price Collapse Is Really Telling Us
Cocoa has fallen back to roughly $4,400 per metric ton, a 2 year low and more than 50% below the 2024 peak. The popular explanation is simple..supply recovered, demand weakened, and speculative excess unwound.
That’s directionally true but incomplete. What’s happening is less about cocoa beans alone and more about credit, market structure, and behavioral shifts across the supply chain.
The Headline Story (and Its Limits)
Most commentary points to…
•   Better weather and higher harvest expectations in West Africa
•   Demand destruction after record prices in 2024
•   Manufacturers cutting back and funds exiting longs
All valid. But none explain the speed or severity of the move on their own.
The Demand Signal That Actually Matters
The cleanest measure of real demand is grindings (processing volumes)…
•   Europe: down 8% YoY (Q4 2025)
•   Asia: down 5% YoY
•   North America: roughly flat
Europe is the key market and it blinked hard. That confirms real demand weakness. But grindings are lagging data. They tell you what already broke, not what happens next.
What the Crowd Is Missing
This Is a Credit & Financing Event
Cocoa doesn’t move without financing…
•   In Ghana, changes to pre financing left farmers unpaid and beans piling up at ports.
•   In Ivory Coast, the government has stepped in to buy unsold stocks to stabilize incomes.
That’s not a normal surplus. It’s plumbing stress. When financing breaks, prices overshoot.
Demand Destruction May Be Sticky
High prices didn’t just reduce consumption they changed behavior…
•   Recipe reformulation using less cocoa
•   More fillers and substitutes
•   Shrinkflation becoming permanent
Those shifts don’t automatically reverse just because prices fall.
Market Structure Is Amplifying the Move
Cocoa futures are thin and fragile…
•   The 2024 spike drove margin stress and chased out hedgers.
•   When liquidity breaks at the top, price discovery often breaks at the bottom.
This is forced liquidation in a narrow market, not just fundamentals repricing.
The Supply Story Is Internally Conflicted
Near term supply looks better. Structurally, not much has changed…
•   Aging trees
•   Disease risk
•   Climate volatility
•   Now lower farm incomes and less reinvestment
Agricultural cycles often overshoot before those constraints reassert themselves.
First Order vs Second Order Effects
Near term…
•   Disinflationary impulse at the margin
•   Relief for chocolate manufacturers
•   Pressure on West African rural incomes and fiscal flows
Next…
•   Lower prices and unpaid farmers equals less maintenance and weaker future yields
•   More government intervention
•   Higher odds of future instability once demand stabilizes
When the Bear Case Breaks
This framing collapses if…
•    European grindings stabilize or rebound
•   Weather or disease disrupt supply
•   Government stockpiling tightens flows
•   Positioning flips in a thin market
Cocoa doesn’t need a shortage to rally..it needs flow to tighten.
Bottom Line
Cocoa is repricing a fragile supply chain financing system after a speculative blow off. That’s why the move feels violent and why it shouldn’t be mistaken for long term equilibrium.
What to Watch…
•   European grindings
•   Farmer payment and financing conditions
•   Government intervention
•   Weather and disease headlines
•   Futures open interest and volatility

title: Japan Isn’t Losing Control It’s Buying Time Before...
content:
Japan Isn’t Losing Control It’s Buying Time Before the Next Crisis
The JGB Liquidity Index has hit record levels, super long yields are surging, and the narrative is drifting toward system failure. 
Something real is happening but it isn’t a funding crisis or a sudden loss of solvency. What we’re seeing is a regime shift in price setting, liquidity behavior, and volatility transmission after decades of heavy suppression.
More importantly, this shift is deliberate. Japan is trying to buy policy wiggle room ahead of the next downturn..specifically to avoid getting dragged back into a deflationary spiral with no credibility left.
What’s Actually Happening
Liquidity conditions have clearly deteriorated. Bloomberg’s gauge which measures how far yields deviate from levels expected in a well functioning market is at its worst reading on record. Volatility has risen, auctions are more fragile at the long end, and relatively small flows are now producing outsized moves.
That lines up with three concrete changes…
•   The BOJ is reducing bond purchases, stepping back as the dominant, price-insensitive buyer.
•   Political risk has risen after election related fiscal pledges without clear funding plans.
•   Super long bonds (30–40y) have become the stress point, where natural demand is thin and duration risk is hardest to absorb.
None of this is imaginary. But jumping from market functioning is strained to Japan is facing a sovereign liquidity crisis is a category error.
The Strategic Context Most People Miss
Japan’s real fear is losing optionality before the next crisis.
After decades of deflation, Japan finally has modest inflation and wage momentum. If the next global shock hits while the BOJ is still pinned to extreme suppression, markets may no longer believe intervention will work. That’s how deflation returns..suddenly, through a confidence break.
Allowing yields to rise and volatility to reappear now is a way to rebuild credibility and market function, so that when the next crisis arrives Japan can ease aggressively without triggering a currency or confidence accident. Short term instability is the cost of future flexibility.
Why Liquidity Looks So Bad
Foreign investors now account for roughly 65% of monthly JGB trading volume, up from about 12% in 2009. That sounds alarming but it’s misunderstood.
Foreigners dominate turnover, not ownership. The bonds are still largely held by domestic institutions and the BOJ. What’s changed is who sets prices at the margin.
Marginal price setters move faster, run tighter risk limits, and react immediately to volatility. That plugs JGBs into global risk cycles even though Japan’s funding base remains domestic.
At the same time, years of BOJ buying reduced free float, weakened dealer market making, and hollowed out two way liquidity. So when prices are finally allowed to move again, liquidity looks worse..not because the market vanished, but because depth and resiliency were never rebuilt underneath suppression.
The Real Line Japan Can’t Cross
The key risk is yields up and the yen down.
If yields rise because growth and inflation expectations improve, that’s manageable. If yields rise because credibility weakens while the currency falls, financial conditions tighten fast and deflation risk reenters through the back door. That’s the configuration Japan cannot afford.
Bottom Line
Japan’s bond market is relearning how to function after decades of control while deliberately trying to avoid being trapped in the next deflationary snapback.
This matters globally because Japan is no longer a dormant anchor. Its repricing feeds into global duration floors, FX carry trades, portfolio allocation, and volatility regimes everywhere.
What looks like a liquidity scare is really a country buying time and credibility before the next crisis even if it looks messy in the meantime.

title: RT
content:
RT 
@charaninvests
: Denmark's doing something worth paying attention to. 
Their US Treasury holdings just hit a 14 year low at $9 billion, down 30% over the past year. 
But the real story is Akademiker Pension, a major Danish pension fund managing $25 billion in assets, which is dumping all $100 million of its US Treasury position by end of January.​
Why? The fund's basically saying US government credit is broken. 
Their chief investment officer told Bloomberg straight up: 
"the US is basically not a good credit and long-term the US government finances are not sustainable." 
They're citing concerns about fiscal discipline, weak government finances, and rising credit risks under Trump's policies. 
The Greenland tensions didn't help either, he admitted that "certainly did not simplify our decision-making process."
This matters because it's not just one fund. 
Other Danish pension funds are also reducing or exiting their Treasury holdings. 
It signals something bigger, institutional investors are reassessing whether US government debt is still the safe haven investment everyone's assumed for decades.​
The US needs about $1 trillion annually from foreign investors to fund its deficits. 
If demand keeps cooling, Treasury yields have to rise to attract buyers. 
And when Treasury yields rise, everything else gets more expensive mortgages, car loans, credit cards, business borrowing.
 It's inflationary and hits regular Americans in the wallet.​
Treasury Secretary Bessent dismissed it as irrelevant and technically he's right, $100 million is nothing in a $30.8 trillion market. 
But that's missing the point. 
The question isn't whether Denmark breaks the market today. 
It's whether this is the start of a confidence erosion among foreign central banks and institutions. 
If Japan, Switzerland, and other major holders start following Denmark's lead, that cumulative effect actually matters for US borrowing costs.
Denmark's US Treasury holdings are at record lows:
The value of US Treasuries held by Denmark is down to ~$9 billion, the lowest in 14 years.
Over the last year, the country decreased its holdings by -$4 billion, or -30%.
Since the 2016 peak, holdings have more than HALVED.
To put this into perspective, Denmark reflects less than 1% of the European $3.6 trillion ownership of US Treasury securities.
Meanwhile, Danish pension fund AkademikerPension is planning to exit all Treasuries by the end of the month, citing concerns over rising credit risks under President Trump's policies.
Denmark is quietly exiting US debt market. 
- 
The Kobeissi Letter

title: From Tariffs To Terms And The Real Greenland Endga...
content:
From Tariffs To Terms And The Real Greenland Endgame
Stripped of the headlines, this doesn’t read like a territorial grab at all. It looks like a negotiation pivot. Tariffs were the pressure point, NATO is the release valve, and Greenland is the leverage. Bringing the NATO Secretary General into it signals that this is moving from unilateral muscle flexing to a framework everyone can live with and claim credit for.
What The Deal Likely Becomes
In practical terms, the most realistic outcome isn’t ownership, it’s access. More basing rights, expanded infrastructure, deeper missile warning and surveillance integration, and a clearer NATO posture in the Arctic. That “Golden Dome” language points straight at early warning, tracking, and air and missile defense..Greenland’s geography makes it unavoidable in that conversation. Call it shared security, call it collective defense, but the effect is more U.S. and NATO presence without crossing sovereignty red lines.
Why NATO Matters Here
Once NATO is the venue, this stops being about America versus Denmark and starts being about alliance cohesion. It gives Europe cover, keeps Denmark from looking cornered, and lets the U.S. get most of what it wants without lighting a diplomatic fire. That’s usually how these things end: de facto control through access and integration, not de jure ownership.
The Bigger Tell
If this were really about conquest, NATO wouldn’t be anywhere near the room. The fact that it is tells you the endgame is legitimacy, burden sharing, and locking in Arctic advantage..quietly, incrementally, and in a way that’s hard to unwind later.
